name: Kansas
headline_status: Marijuana is illegal in Kansas for both recreational and medical use; only a narrow legal defense covers low-THC CBD oil.
summary: Kansas has no medical or adult-use cannabis program, and a first possession offense is a Class B misdemeanor that can bring jail time. Claire and Lola's Law (2019) only lets people with CBD oil containing up to 5% THC raise an affirmative defense; it does not allow sales. The 2026 session adjourned April 10 without advancing any medical, decriminalization or legalization bill, and Kansas has no citizen initiative process.

possession_limit.value: No amount of marijuana is legal to possess.

penalties.value: First-time possession of any amount is a Class B misdemeanor punishable by up to 6 months in jail and a fine of up to $1,000.

medical_program.value: None. Claire and Lola's Law (SB 28, 2019) gives an affirmative defense for possessing CBD oil with up to 5% THC, which prevents conviction but not arrest, and does not permit sales or production.

retail_sales.value: No legal marijuana sales of any kind.

hemp_thc.value: CBD products with little to no THC are generally sold legally. New federal hemp limits, most of which take effect on 11 December 2026, are expected to remove most consumable hemp-derived THC products from shelves.

purchase_age.value: No legal purchase of marijuana for any age; there are no licensed adult-use or medical marijuana sales.

public_use.value: Not allowed anywhere: there is no legal recreational or medical marijuana use, so using it in public or private can lead to possession charges.

tourists.value: No. There are no legal marijuana sales, out-of-state medical cards are not recognized, and visitors face the same possession penalties as residents.

home_grow.value: Not allowed; there is no legal way to grow marijuana in Kansas.

dui.value: Impairment-based: Kansas has no THC per se or zero-tolerance law, so a cannabis DUI requires evidence of impairment.

timeline.event: Claire and Lola's Law (SB 28) creates an affirmative defense for low-THC CBD oil
House passes the first of three medical cannabis bills (2021, 2022, 2023); none advance in the Senate
Legislature adjourns without acting on medical (SB 294), decriminalization (SB 295) or legalization (HB 2405) bills

faq.a: No. Kansas allows neither recreational nor medical marijuana, and possessing any amount is a crime.

faq.q: What is the penalty for marijuana possession in Kansas?
faq.a: A first offense is a Class B misdemeanor punishable by up to 6 months in jail and a $1,000 fine.
CBD with little or no THC is generally sold legally. CBD oil with up to 5% THC is covered only by an affirmative defense in court.

faq.q: Can Kansas voters legalize marijuana by ballot?
faq.a: No. Kansas has no statewide citizen initiative process, so any change has to come from the legislature.
